title: ADR-0021: mods add to the screen and guard nothing

content.summary: Mods are an **additive** layer: a mod keeps a session's signals on screen, and nothing may require one. belt stays the only guard a rule may rely on, because a mod fails open.
content.meta: 2026-10-05 · decision record · accepted, Claude-only clause superseded by ADR-0023

cols.label: planned mods listed from the start

blocks.text: This architecture decision record (ADR) puts mods at `mods/<name>/`, one complete plugin per directory. The root marketplace `thismoon` lists them. They are additive only: no skill, hook, or service may require a mod.
It changes things for two groups. A person who builds a mod may show anything and may enforce nothing. A person who writes a rule keeps it in belt.

sections.h: belt fails closed where a mod fails open

blocks.text: The table shows why belt keeps the rules: belt fails closed, and a mod that throws or times out is skipped, so it fails open.

cols: A rule may rely on it
rows: Skipped on a throw or a timeout

items: belt is the guard layer. It fails closed, and it is the only enforcement a rule may rely on.
A mod is a module hook. Claude Code skips it on a throw or a timeout, so a guard written as a mod fails open.
Codex and pi never load a mod at all. Anything they need stays a skill.

sections.h: A mod watches the same events belt guards

blocks.caption: How a mod sits beside belt.

steps.caption: Claude Code emits an event on every turn and every tool call.
belt checks the tool call and fails closed.
A mod observes the same events, and a throw or a timeout skips it.
The mod draws a band above the prompt or opens a pane.
A probe of a localhost service stays silent when the service is down.

blocks.text: Look at the two arrows that leave Claude Code. The one to belt can stop a tool call. The one to the mod only feeds the screen.

A session already carries signals nobody sees: belt's PreToolUse denials, worklog keys, work-on phase markers in answers, and present page ids in tool results. Before mods they reached the person only by being read back.

sections.h: A mod may deny in two cases only

items: The first case is the user's own Cancel in a hold dialog.
The second case is a convenience guard. Such a guard fails open, is off by a config key, and duplicates no belt guard.
A mod never edits the transcript.
A mod may change the model of a subagent spawn only behind a config key. It does so only when the caller set no model or a model the key lists, and never for a model the caller chose explicitly.

sections.h: A merge to main deploys a mod, with no release line

blocks.text: Mods are not components. They have no Makefile, no release-please entry, and no tag line of their own. The version sits in `plugin.json`.
Loading is machine-private, as ADR-0006 already says of recipes. The consuming repo registers the marketplace from the ralph sources cache and enables mods through `enabledPlugins`.
Skills, hooks, and services are unchanged. A machine with no mods enabled behaves exactly as before.

sections.h: The price is a check CI cannot run and an API that moves

items: Continuous integration (CI) runs the mods' `node --test` suites and checks every mod is in the marketplace. It cannot run the plugin validation, because the runner has no Claude Code binary. A hook the engine would refuse is caught on the author's machine.
The plugin API is early access and moves between releases. The generated `.claude-plugin/types/` beside a loaded mod is the authority.
Codex and pi see nothing of this layer.

blocks.text: A release that renames an event breaks the band **silently**, until someone runs it with the debug flag.

items: The consuming repo registers the marketplace and enables mods through `enabledPlugins`.
The author of a mod runs the plugin validation before each push, because CI cannot.
Anyone who relies on the Claude-only clause reads ADR-0023 first, because it supersedes that clause.
